name: James Lawson
aliases: James Morris Lawson Jr.; Rev. James Lawson
description: James Morris Lawson Jr., born 22 September 1928 in Uniontown, Pennsylvania, was an American Methodist pastor and the leading theoretician and tactician of nonviolence in the civil rights movement. The son and grandson of ministers, he was licensed to preach in high school, jailed as a Korean War draft conscientious objector, and spent three years as a missionary in India studying Gandhi's methods. At Vanderbilt Divinity School in Nashville he ran nonviolence workshops that trained John Lewis, Diane Nash, Bernard Lafayette and other students who led the 1960 Nashville sit-ins; Vanderbilt expelled him for that activism, and Nashville became the first major Southern city to desegregate its downtown. He served as the Southern Christian Leadership Conference's director of nonviolent education, and as a Memphis pastor he invited Martin Luther King Jr. to support the 1968 sanitation workers' strike, the campaign in which King was assassinated. From 1974 to 1999 he pastored Holman United Methodist Church in Los Angeles, taught nonviolence for two decades, and returned to Vanderbilt as a distinguished professor. He died on 9 June 2024 in Los Angeles, aged 95.

name: Jo Ann Boyce
aliases: Jo Ann Allen Boyce; Jo Ann Allen
description: Jo Ann Allen Boyce, born 15 September 1941 in Clinton, Tennessee, was one of the Clinton Twelve, the Black teenagers who in August 1956 became among the first to desegregate a public high school in the American South. After the Supreme Court's Brown decision and a federal court order, Boyce, then a 14-year-old sophomore, and eleven classmates enrolled at previously all-white Clinton High School, ending the twenty-mile bus ride to a segregated school in Knoxville. The students met hostile crowds, slurs and thrown objects, while segregationist agitators and Ku Klux Klan members drove violent protests that brought the National Guard to Clinton. Boyce was elected vice president of her homeroom, but by December 1956 the danger drove her family to relocate to Los Angeles; only two of the Twelve remained to graduate from Clinton. Boyce built a long career as a pediatric nurse, spoke to students across the country about the Clinton experience, and in 2019 co-authored, with Debbie Levy, the verse memoir for young readers This Promise of Change. She died at her Los Angeles home on 3 December 2025, aged 84, after living with pancreatic cancer for a decade.

name: Julian Bond
description: Horace Julian Bond, born 14 January 1940 in Nashville, Tennessee, was a civil rights leader, Georgia legislator, professor and writer. The son of educator Horace Mann Bond, he attended Morehouse College in Atlanta, where in 1960 he helped found the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee and served as its communications director, leaving college to work full time in the movement before completing his degree in 1971. Elected to the Georgia House of Representatives in 1965, he was denied his seat by legislators who objected to his opposition to the Vietnam War; the U.S. Supreme Court ruled unanimously in Bond v. Floyd that his exclusion was unconstitutional, and he took his seat in 1967. He served twenty years in the Georgia House and Senate, co-founded the Southern Poverty Law Center in 1971 and served as its first president, and narrated the landmark PBS documentary series Eyes on the Prize. From 1998 to 2010 he chaired the NAACP, and he taught history at the University of Virginia from 1992 until retiring in 2012, teaching more than five thousand students. Bond died on 15 August 2015 in Fort Walton Beach, Florida, aged 75.

name: Justin Fields
description: Justin Skyler Fields, born March 5, 1999, in Kennesaw, Georgia, is an American professional football quarterback now with the Kansas City Chiefs. After a freshman season at Georgia, he transferred to Ohio State, where in 2019 and 2020 he twice won Big Ten Offensive Player of the Year and led the Buckeyes to the 2021 College Football Playoff National Championship Game. The Chicago Bears selected him eleventh overall in the 2021 NFL Draft. In Chicago from 2021 to 2023 he set the NFL single-game regular-season record for quarterback rushing yards with 178 and became the third quarterback to rush for 1,000 yards in a season. Traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2024, he mostly served as a backup, then signed with the New York Jets in March 2025 and started nine games that season, throwing for 1,259 yards and seven touchdowns with one interception and four rushing scores before a knee injury ended his year. In March 2026 the Jets traded him to Kansas City, his fourth NFL team.

name: Jeremiah Brown
description: Jeremiah Brown, born 5 May 2000 in Seattle, Washington, is an American model and reality television personality. He worked as a model from 2018, seven years before his television debut, with campaigns for brands including Adidas, True Religion and Nordstrom, and he studied film at Central Washington University before relocating to Los Angeles. In June 2025 he entered the villa as an original Islander on the seventh season of Peacock's Love Island USA, coupling first with Huda Mustafa and later, after a public vote, with Iris. He was dumped from the villa on Day 16, in nineteenth place. After the season he worked as a model, hosted a book club on social media, and joined the cast of the second season of Love Island: Beyond the Villa in 2026, discussing his modelling, reading and streaming work in a September 2026 interview.

name: Jamie Broadnax
description: Jamie Broadnax is an American writer, podcaster, and the creator of Black Girl Nerds, the online publication and multimedia space she founded in February 2012 for Black women and other nerdy women of color. Blogging since 2007, she created the site the same evening a search for the phrase 'Black Girl Nerds' returned nothing, reasoning that if no space existed for women like her, she would build one. In a 2013 interview she described Black Girl Nerds as an inclusive fellowship around geek fandoms — comics, anime, cosplay, technology, and popular culture — where Black women could be themselves without having their Blackness questioned for their interests. The publication's own author page identifies her as its creator, a member of the Critics Choice Association, and executive producer of the Black Girl Nerds Podcast, and notes her appearance on MSNBC's Melissa Harris-Perry Show and her place on The Grio's Top 100. Podcast listings show her still hosting and editing the Black Girl Nerds podcast in September 2026, including its 2026 Toronto International Film Festival coverage, more than fourteen years after she founded the community for blerds — Black nerds — to find fellowship.

name: Jimmy Cliff
description: Jimmy Cliff, born James Chambers on July 30, 1944, in St. James Parish, Jamaica, was the reggae pioneer who carried Jamaica's music to the world as a singer, songwriter, and actor. He emerged from Kingston's music scene in the early 1960s, after a childhood first hit, Hurricane Hattie, written as a teenager. By 1970 he had three singles in the United Kingdom charts, among them Wonderful World, Beautiful People and Vietnam, which Bob Dylan praised as a great protest song. He starred as Ivanhoe Martin in the landmark 1972 film The Harder They Come, whose soundtrack helped popularize reggae internationally, and later reached new audiences with I Can See Clearly Now for the 1993 film Cool Runnings. He won two Grammy Awards for best reggae album, was nominated seven times, held Jamaica's Order of Merit, and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2010, the only Jamaican besides Bob Marley so honored at his death. Cliff died on November 24, 2025, at eighty-one, after a seizure followed by pneumonia, his wife Latifa Chambers announced.

name: John Henrik Clarke
description: John Henrik Clarke, born January 1, 1915, in Union Springs, Alabama, to a sharecropper family, was a principally self-trained historian, Pan-Africanist, and pioneer in the formation of Africana studies in the United States. He left the South in 1932, traveling by boxcar through Chicago to New York City, where in Harlem he studied African history under the tutelage of scholar Arthur A. Schomburg while working full time, and later studied at New York University and the New School for Social Research. In 1949 the New School asked him to teach in its new African Studies Center. He founded the African Heritage Studies Association in 1968, was principally responsible for creating the Black and Puerto Rican Studies Department at Hunter College, where he was professor of African and Puerto Rican Studies from 1970 to 1985 and emeritus on retirement, and lectured at Cornell University as a distinguished visiting professor. His works include A New Approach to African History and African People in World History; he also contributed to the Chicago Defender. He died July 16, 1998, in New York City.

name: Jasmine Crockett
description: Jasmine Felicia Crockett is an American attorney and politician who has represented Texas's 30th congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives since January 3, 2023. Born March 29, 1981, in St. Louis, Missouri, she graduated from the Mary Institute and Saint Louis Country Day School in 1999, earned a B.A. from Rhodes College in Memphis in 2003, attended the Thurgood Marshall School of Law at Texas Southern University, and received her J.D. from the University of Houston Law Center in 2006. She worked in private practice and served as a public defender in Bowie County, Texas, from 2007 to 2010, later practicing as a civil rights and criminal defense attorney. A Democrat, she represented the 100th district in the Texas House of Representatives from 2021 to 2023 before her election to Congress. Her official House biography describes a career directed at protecting the civil liberties of underrepresented communities, records her membership in Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated, and identifies her as the first Black woman elected Freshman Leadership Representative. In the 118th Congress she served on the Oversight and Accountability and Agriculture committees.

name: Jim Kelly
description: James Milton Kelly was an American martial artist, actor, and athlete, identified in reference accounts as the first Black martial arts film star. Born May 5, 1946, in Paris, Kentucky, he competed in basketball, football, and track at Bourbon County High School and attended the University of Louisville on a football scholarship before leaving in his freshman year. He began studying karate in Kentucky in 1964, earned his black belt in San Diego five years later, and in 1971 won four championships, including the world middleweight title at the Long Beach International Karate Championships. He opened his own studio in Los Angeles. His first film role was in Melinda (1972); his breakout came as Williams, opposite Bruce Lee, in Enter the Dragon (1973), which led to a three-film contract with Warner Bros. He starred as the title character in Black Belt Jones (1974) and as Mister Keyes in Three the Hard Way (1974), and later headlined Black Samurai (1977). He also played professional tennis on the USTA senior circuit in later years. Kelly died of cancer on June 29, 2013, at his home in San Diego, California, aged 67.

name: John Primer
description: John Primer is an American Chicago blues singer, guitarist, and songwriter. Born March 5, 1945, in Camden, Mississippi, he grew up in a sharecropping family in Madison County and moved to Chicago in 1963 at age eighteen, playing for tips at the Maxwell Street market. From 1974 he played seven nights a week in the house band at Theresa's Lounge on Chicago's South Side, backing Junior Wells and other blues artists. Willie Dixon recruited him into the Chicago Blues All-Stars in 1979. In 1980 he joined Muddy Waters's band as guitarist, bandleader, and opening act, remaining until Waters's death in 1983. He then spent thirteen years with Magic Slim and the Teardrops as guitarist and bandleader. Primer's solo recording career began with Poor Man's Blues and Stuff You Got to Watch, both in 1991, followed by The Real Deal in 1995, and in 2008 he founded his own Blues House Productions imprint. He was inducted into the Chicago Blues Hall of Fame in 2017. KNKX Public Radio, recording him in session in August 2026, credited him with seventeen albums of his own and performances on hundreds more.

name: Josephine St. Pierre Ruffin
aliases: Josephine St. Pierre; Mrs. George L. Ruffin
description: Josephine St. Pierre Ruffin was a Boston publisher, journalist, suffragist, and civil-rights organizer born in Boston on August 31, 1842, and deceased March 13, 1924, in Boston. During the Civil War she recruited Black men for the 54th and 55th Massachusetts regiments. Afterward she worked in Massachusetts suffrage organizations, ran voter outreach in Beacon Hill and the West End in 1885, and helped found the West End Suffrage League in 1887. In 1893 she co-founded the Woman's Era Club with her daughter Florida Ruffin Ridley, Maria Louise Baldwin, Ida B. Wells, and others. She edited and published its publication, The Woman's Era, described as the first national newspaper created by and for Black women. With her daughter, she organized the First National Conference of Colored Women in Boston in 1895, drawing 100 women from twenty clubs. The conference created an umbrella organization later associated with the National Association of Colored Women's Clubs. In 1910 she helped found the Boston chapter of the NAACP.

name: Julie Dash
description: Julie Dash is an American filmmaker, author and producer associated with the L.A. Rebellion, the generation of African and African American filmmakers who studied at UCLA and built an alternative to Hollywood cinema. Born in Queens, New York, she studied at City College of New York and the AFI Conservatory before earning an MFA in film and television production from UCLA in 1985. Her early shorts — Four Women (1975), Diary of an African Nun (1977) and Illusions (1982), on which UCLA credits her as director, producer, writer and editor — centred Black women's interior lives and Hollywood's racial illusions. Her debut feature, Daughters of the Dust (1991), about a Gullah Geechee family on the Sea Islands in 1902 weighing migration to the mainland, became the first feature by an African American woman to receive a general theatrical release in the United States, and entered the National Film Registry in 2004. Dash later directed for television, including The Rosa Parks Story (2002) and episodes of Queen Sugar and Women of the Movement in 2021–2022, extending her historical, women-centred storytelling across formats and into museum and teaching work at Spelman College in Atlanta, Georgia.

name: Jamila Trimuel
description: Jamila Trimuel is the founder and CEO of Ladies of Virtue (LOV), the Chicago nonprofit she founded in 2011 that prepares Black girls ages 9–24 to become confident, purpose-driven leaders through mentorship, leadership training and community service, serving more than 2,000 girls and women annually. Her recognitions include Obama Administration Change Agent honors with an invitation to the 2016 White House United State of Women Summit, selection as a 2023 PepsiCo Changemaker, and TEDx speaking. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Janella Curtis
description: Janella Curtis is the founder and CEO of Notary Nook, her Chicago notary and loan-signing practice — she is an Illinois-commissioned notary public, a remote online notary and a certified loan signing agent with 250+ completed signings on her professional profile — and the creator of NookScan Protocol, a patent-pending, AI-powered document-compliance platform she describes as designed to catch errors before execution; in a published statement she dates founding both in August 2025. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Jessica Barnes
description: Jessica Barnes is Senior Counsel at Gordon Rees Scully Mansukhani (GRSM), the national Am Law 100 law firm founded in 1974 and described as the first and only firm with offices in all 50 states. Her role is documented on WVON's Class of 2026 roster; no firm biography or other independent source for this Jessica Barnes was located in this pass, and other attorneys of the same name (including in Pittsburgh and Orange County) were excluded as namesakes. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Joy Joshua
description: Joy Joshua is the founder of Journey & Thingz, the Chicago mobile arts business she launched in 2022 offering jewelry-making, art and STEM workshops for schools, community programming, private events and corporate team-building; WVON's roster credits her as Founder & Creative Director. She also works as a Food Education Program Assistant for the 61st Street Farmers Market at Experimental Station, the Woodlawn nonprofit whose profile of the market recounts her business's launch. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.
